edges.mechanism: Unknown mechanism; lithium plus classic psychedelics associated with seizures; chronic lithium also subjectively intensified LSD responses.
edges.evidence: 47% of 62 online lithium+psychedelic reports involved seizures (39% medical attention) vs 0 of 34 lamotrigine reports; adolescent case of 3 generalized seizures after LSD on low-dose lithium; retrospective questionnaire. Low certainty but serious signal.

edges.mechanism: Chronic SSRI exposure (5-HT2A downregulation/serotonergic adaptation) attenuates LSD subjective effects; CYP2D6-inhibiting SSRIs (paroxetine) raise LSD exposure.
edges.evidence: 88% of 32 chronic SSRI users reported attenuated/eliminated LSD effects (retrospective); phase I RCT: paroxetine reduced bad effects/anxiety/nausea, raised LSD Cmax/AUC 1.4/1.5-fold, no QTc change; DDI systematic review.

edges.mechanism: Chronic TCA use associated with subjectively increased physical, hallucinatory and psychological LSD responses.
edges.evidence: Retrospective questionnaire study (small n); very low certainty.

edges.mechanism: Chronic MAOI use associated with subjectively decreased LSD effects; serotonergic pharmacodynamic interaction.
edges.evidence: Retrospective questionnaire study; DDI systematic review reports both attenuation and potentiation across classes; very low certainty.

edges.mechanism: CYP2D6 contributes to LSD metabolism (nor-LSD formation); inhibition increases LSD exposure and may prolong effects.
edges.evidence: Phase I RCT with paroxetine (GMR Cmax 1.4, AUC 1.5); in vitro CYP phenotyping. Extension to other strong inhibitors is inference.

edges.mechanism: Absent CYP2D6 function prolongs LSD half-life and raises exposure.
edges.evidence: Pooled analysis of 81 subjects: ~75% higher LSD and O-H-LSD AUC, stronger/longer subjective effects; microdose PK study: 2 of 4 anxiety withdrawals had intermediate/weak CYP2D6 activity.

edges.mechanism: Rifampicin induced formation of LSD metabolites in hepatocyte-derived cells; may reduce LSD exposure.
edges.evidence: In vitro only; no human data; very low certainty.

edges.mechanism: 5-HT2A antagonist blocks (pretreatment) or reverses (post-dose) LSD effects and reduces cardiovascular effects without altering LSD PK.
edges.evidence: Two RCTs in healthy volunteers; used as planned or rescue option in research.

edges.mechanism: Dopamine/5-HT2A antagonism; risperidone reported to aggravate HPPD symptoms after hallucinogen use.
edges.evidence: Case reports/series summarized in HPPD treatment SR; DDI systematic review; low certainty.

edges.mechanism: 5-HT2A agonism can precipitate psychotic symptoms; higher risk with schizophrenia or genetic vulnerability.
edges.evidence: MA: psychosis incidence 0.6% in RCTs, 3.8% long-lasting symptoms in UCTs including schizophrenia; trial SAEs included psychosis; twin study shows interaction with schizophrenia genetic vulnerability.

edges.mechanism: Psychedelic-associated (hypo)mania, especially bipolar I and familial vulnerability.
edges.evidence: SR/MA: 5.8% (trials) to 30% (naturalistic bipolar samples); population cohort HR 5.97 for incident mania after hallucinogen acute care; twin study gene-environment interaction.

edges.mechanism: Dose-dependent sympathomimetic increases in blood pressure, heart rate and body temperature.
edges.evidence: Pooled analysis of 83 healthy subjects (no SBP >180 mmHg; HR >100 in 25% at 200 ug); dose-response RCT; AUD MA notes transient BP increases. Uncontrolled hypertension excluded from trials.

edges.mechanism: LSD is a high-affinity 5-HT2B agonist; chronic 5-HT2B activation is the mechanism of drug-induced valvulopathy (fenfluramine, ergots). Concern centres on repeated/chronic microdosing.
edges.evidence: SR: no clinical LSD valvulopathy cases, preclinical fibrotic signalling; mouse chronic microdose study negative; open-label human echo study (n=19, 8 wk) normal; 5-HT2B review: cumulative risk uncharacterized.

edges.mechanism: Unknown developmental risk; early animal data showed abortions/stillbirths after early-pregnancy injection.
edges.evidence: Scoping review: 11 LSD human sources (1968-2020), small and confounded; rat study 1967. Very low certainty; absence of data is not evidence of safety.

edges.mechanism: Convulsive episodes reported among SAEs in patient trials; seizure signal with lithium co-use.
edges.evidence: SR/MA of AEs; online report analysis; low certainty.

edges.mechanism: Prior HPPD/flashbacks may recur or worsen; SSRIs and risperidone reported to exacerbate.
edges.evidence: Case reports and HPPD treatment SR; pooled healthy-subject data (6 transient flashbacks).

edges.mechanism: Common recreational co-use; no controlled LSD-cannabis interaction data; potential additive psychoactive effects.
edges.evidence: Global Psychedelic Survey: cannabis and alcohol most common co-used substances; no interaction studies. Very low certainty.

edges.mechanism: Cross-reactivity causes false-positive CEDIA LSD screens with sertraline, ambroxol and bupropion; confirm by chromatography/MS.
edges.evidence: Case reports/letters and review of immunoassay interferences.
